setup.name.title: What will you call the agent?
setup.name.agent.label: Agent name
setup.name.owner.label: Your name
setup.name.owner.placeholder: what the agent should call you
setup.name.explain.constitution.title: The name goes into the constitution
setup.name.explain.constitution.text: It becomes part of who the agent understands themselves to be, and it is the name their words appear under, in the window and in Telegram.
setup.name.explain.owner.title: The agent needs your name
setup.name.explain.owner.text: So they know whose word is final when instructions conflict, and can address you like a person.
setup.constitution.title: Constitution
setup.constitution.explain.root.title: This is the agent's root
setup.constitution.explain.root.text: Who they are, why, how they are built, what they will not do and who they are loyal to. Everything else in them can change on its own; this text changes only with you.
setup.constitution.explain.edit.title: Read it and correct it
setup.constitution.explain.edit.text: This is the standard text, but it is yours. If something is not about your agent, rewrite it right here: they will take it as their own the first time they start.
setup.constitution.accept.label: I accept this constitution
setup.constitution.error.not_accepted: Accept the constitution first: the toggle on the left
setup.keys.title: Where the model comes from
setup.keys.lead: The model is the only thing the agent takes from outside. Everything else stays on this computer.
setup.keys.money: Money, plainly: with an API key you pay per answer as you go, and there is no cap. A ChatGPT subscription is a flat fee, but it only allows so many requests a week. A local model is free, but it runs on your own hardware.
setup.keys.provider.api.title: OpenAI API key
setup.keys.provider.anthropic.text: Anthropic, Z.ai, MiniMax, Kimi and compatible ones
setup.keys.provider.chatgpt.title: ChatGPT subscription
setup.keys.provider.local.title: Local model
setup.keys.provider.local.text: Ollama or LM Studio on this computer
setup.keys.explain.api.title: Why a key
setup.keys.explain.api.text: It is kept only in the settings file on this computer and goes nowhere else. Any OpenAI-compatible address and model will work.
setup.keys.explain.anthropic.title: One protocol, six doors
setup.keys.explain.anthropic.text: The check asks the server for its list of models, when the server has one.
setup.keys.relay.status.authorized: Signed in — this carries over into the installed program
setup.keys.relay.status.pending: Waiting for the browser sign-in. If the tab closed, press again to start over.
setup.keys.explain.chatgpt.title: How this works
setup.keys.explain.chatgpt.text: The built-in relay talks to ChatGPT on your subscription. Signing in opens the browser; your sign-in then carries over into the installed program.
setup.keys.explain.local.title: Everything stays here
setup.keys.explain.local.text: Ollama or LM Studio on this computer. There is no key, and nothing leaves for the network. The model must already be downloaded.
setup.keys.effort.title: Reasoning effort
setup.keys.effort.unsupported: no effort level is sent to this model
setup.keys.effort.text: How much the model thinks before answering: more effort means a slower and costlier answer (reasoning is billed as output tokens). This can be changed in settings.
setup.keys.telegram.title: Telegram, if you need it
setup.keys.telegram.token.label: Bot token
setup.keys.telegram.owner_id.label: Your Telegram id
setup.keys.telegram.text: without it the agent cannot tell which of the people writing to them is you. You can leave this empty.
setup.keys.error.local_base_url: A local model address is needed
setup.keys.error.relay_not_signed_in: You are not signed in to ChatGPT — without that the agent has nothing to answer with. Press “Next” again if you will sign in later, in settings.
setup.keys.error.telegram_id: Telegram also needs your id: a number
setup.keys.models.missing: Model “${current.trim() || "…"}” is not in the list. Available:
setup.keys.models.more: and ${models.length - shown.length} more — type the name yourself
setup.mode.title: What is the agent allowed to do?
setup.mode.lead: Three questions, and they are independent: how far the agent reaches, whether to install the Windows service, and whether to give them windows and a mouse.
setup.mode.install_note.sandbox: Folders outside it that the agent should see are added later, in settings.
setup.mode.install_note.interactive: The agent asks for them separately, in a Windows prompt, when a particular action needs them.
setup.mode.service.note: Windows will ask for administrator rights once: only an administrator can register a service.
setup.mode.service.no_admin: This account has no administrator rights, and only an administrator can register a Windows service. Ask an administrator to run the installer — or install without the service: both fences work without it, and the service can be added later, in settings.
setup.mode.session0.off: Off for now: the agent lives in your session and sees the desktop. If you turn it on, they get system rights but stop seeing the desktop, and a weak model may not understand what it is doing.
setup.mode.computer.note: No administrator rights are needed. All four rights are granted at once; you can narrow them in settings.
setup.mode.computer.off: Off for now: the `computer` hand is there, but there is no body under it — call it and it just says no.
setup.mode.foot: In the sandbox that is their whole world — the only thing they can break is themselves.
setup.install.head: Ready to install
setup.install.model_chatgpt: ChatGPT subscription through the built-in relay
setup.install.installed_tail: — this is an update: memory, constitution and settings will stay
setup.install.service_yes: install — Windows will ask for administrator rights
setup.install.service_no: do not install — the program runs from its window
setup.install.computer_on: turn on — the agent gets windows, screen, keyboard and mouse; the rights can be narrowed in settings
setup.install.computer_off: leave off — you can turn it on later, in settings
setup.install.log_hint: The report is also written to install.log next to the installer.
setup.install.service_stopped: The service is installed but did not start: the details are in the service log.
setup.install.service_absent: The service was not installed: administrator rights were not given.
setup.install.service_missing: The service was not installed: this package has no helene-svc.exe.
setup.install.open_failed: Could not open {product}: {error}. They live in {dir} — use the desktop shortcut.
setup.legacy.start_auto: starts by itself at every boot
setup.legacy.account_system: runs as SYSTEM — the highest rights on this computer
setup.legacy.head: An earlier version still lives here
setup.legacy.lead_one: Windows says the service “{name}” is still registered — it never went away.
setup.legacy.lead_many: Windows says that services of earlier versions are registered here. It is the same product under its former names: removing the previous version deleted the files but left the service.
setup.legacy.why_bad_title: Why it gets in the way
setup.legacy.why_bad_body: Such a service runs as the system and starts a program from a folder an ordinary user writes into: anything that can write to that folder as you gets system rights at the next boot. And one more thing: its relay holds the same local port the new agent is configured for — the new agent would then go and talk to the old relay, on someone else's subscription, and all you would see is “the model did not answer”.
setup.legacy.optional_body: Until you press the button, the installer does nothing to it.
setup.legacy.uac_notice: Windows will ask for administrator rights.
setup.legacy.remove_failed: {error} — remove it by hand: sc.exe stop {name} and sc.exe delete {name}
setup.uninstall.head: Remove {product}
setup.uninstall.lead: The program, the service, the shortcuts and the entry in “Installed apps” will be deleted. What to do with the agent's data is yours to decide.
setup.uninstall.keep_body: a note named HOW-TO-COME-BACK.md will be left beside it
setup.uninstall.purge_body: close this window and run `helene-setup.exe --export` next to the program — it builds an archive you can carry to a new machine — and only then come back and remove.
setup.uninstall.keep_text: memory, constitution, model key, Telegram and ChatGPT sign-ins stay in the data folder
setup.uninstall.purge_text: the data folder goes with the program, there will be nothing to restore
